question.text: 'Ganga Infra Trust' has four LPs with commitments: Mr. A - INR 50 crore, Ms. B - INR 30 crore, Mr. C - INR 15 crore, Ms. D - INR 5 crore. Total commitment is INR 100 crore. A drawdown notice for 20% of commitments is issued. How much must Ms. B wire?

explanation.text: The Logic: Ms. B's drawdown = 20% x INR 30 crore = INR 6 crore. Pro-rata based on her individual commitment, independent of other LPs' shares. The Trap: INR 3 cr uses 10%. INR 4 cr is off-by-one. INR 10 cr confuses with the total drawdown (INR 20 crore) or Mr. A's share. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same pro-ration. XIX-D adds default/recycle twists. Manager's Pro-Tip: Always compute each LP's draw independently based on THEIR commitment, not on the total pool - pro-rata math is additive, not divisional.
